questions.q: Why do the metrics in the tracked run carry prefixes such as train_ and test_?
options: MLflow refuses metrics without a prefix
So nobody has to guess which data split a number was measured on
The prefix makes the metric faster to query
It converts the metric into a tag
questions.explain: MLflow accepts any metric name. The prefix is a discipline of ours: a bare 'auc' could be train, test or something else entirely.

questions.q: What happened when the same run tried to log parameter C a second time with a different value?
options: The new value silently replaced the old one
Both values were stored as a list
MLflow raised an exception saying changing param values is not allowed
The run was marked FAILED and deleted
questions.explain: Params are immutable within a run, so a recorded setting cannot change without you noticing. Tags, by contrast, can be edited.

questions.q: The C=-1 run raised an error inside a with mlflow.start_run() block. What did MLflow store?
options: Nothing, the run vanished
A run with status FAILED that remains searchable
A run with status FINISHED and empty metrics
A run that was retried automatically with C=1
questions.explain: The with block ends the run with status FAILED when an exception escapes. We filtered on status = 'FINISHED' to exclude it when comparing.

questions.q: Autolog reported a training accuracy of 0.889 on the churn pipeline. Why is that number not impressive?
options: Only about 11 percent of customers cancel, so predicting that nobody cancels also scores 0.889
Accuracy is always about 0.889 for logistic regression
Autolog rounds accuracy to three digits
It was measured on the test set
questions.explain: With a cancel rate of 0.111, the no-skill answer is 88.9 percent accurate. Autolog's metrics were also all on training data, so log your own test metrics.

questions.q: Why did we keep C=1.0 when C=10 and C=100 scored the same test ROC AUC of 0.744?
options: Larger C values are not allowed in scikit-learn
C=1.0 had a higher train AUC
It is the simplest setting that ties for best, and nothing improves beyond it
MLflow only stores the first run it sees
questions.explain: The sweep plateaued at 0.744. When settings tie, prefer the simpler, more regularized one, and record why in the run's tags or notes.
